title: Mapping Stellar Obliquity Across Space and Time [Astrophysics]
originalMonograph: Mapping Stellar Obliquity Across Space and Time
summary: Mapping Stellar Obliquity Across Space and Time: New Evidence in Space & Astronomy: The angle between a star's rotational angular momentum vector and the orbital angular momentum vector of its planets---stellar obliquity---encodes the initial conditions and dynamical history of planetary systems. Variations in obliquity with orbital separation may arise from either primordial disk structure (e.g., broken or warped protoplanetary disks with misaligned inner and outer regions) or subsequent dynamical interactions with planets or external perturbers. Published via arXiv Open Science Wire (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40527v1).
